<meta>This is the opening page of the Latin translation of the "Liber de compositione alchimiae," a foundational text in the history of alchemy. It establishes the legendary lineage of the art, linking it to Hermes Trismegistus and the translation from Arabic into Latin.</meta>

# The moving prologue begins.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, here begins the book of a certain <term>alchemy</term> <note>original: "alkamie"</note> which Morienus the Roman produced for King Khalid of Egypt, and which Hermes, by his authority, translated from Arabic into Latin as the prologue of this book.

<margin>Almand</margin>
<margin>Adris <note>Idris</note>, Morienus, the translator of the law of ancient histories and divine arts, was a philosopher.</margin>
Because they called the first of them by such a name, and he was Enoch, who by another name was called Hermes, and by another name <term>Idris</term> in Arabic; the second was Noah, who similarly is called by another name Hermes and by another name in Arabic. In their time, however, there was a Hermes who reigned in Egypt after the flood and worked in that same Egypt for a long time. This man, however, years before the passing of the world—namely, he is a god <note>likely referring to the deification of Hermes/Thoth</note>—was a collector of the skill of virtues for himself, namely for the sake of God's grace of reason; in him was the truth of <unclear>xph</unclear> philosophy. He was a philosopher skilled in all the arts and disciplines, both liberal and mechanical, and was the first inventor and author of them after the flood. For the things which came after were recorded in his name; they wished to follow in his footsteps, which is called the <term>Treatise of Hermes</term>. He brought back to memory his long and divine book regarding the Great Art or the treatise of the <term>azores</term> <note>possibly referring to "azoth" or a specific alchemical preparation</note>, which he brought back to form, extracted by the revelation of our Lord, not received in the Lord by study or by the effort of showing or explaining how the thing might be held. But for this reason, he also has the name inscribed in the prologue of the treatise, he who rendered this book by his own intention. For this is a divine book, filled with divine things, full and not disguised in the reason of its work, as if it were not born in the land of the prophet, so to speak grammatically. In this book, moreover, one studies to understand fully the living, true, and right way, not a servile way; insufficiencies cannot provide that. For on account of this, the book of <term>Morienus</term> on <term>alchemy</term> <note>original: "elkimie"</note>—which is called alchemy for its own reason, just as matter is said to have generated matters in the beginning—that name was placed there for the ignorant, or according to a wonderful and difficult reason it is revealed. Hermes says that he wants it to be <gloss>concerning the matter</gloss> of <term>alchemy</term>, and he defined the terms therein. For he says in the book revealed upon the <unclear>muracõe</unclear> treatise: Alchemy is the mistress of the body from one proper kind, which works and profits... <note>The text here becomes highly technical and abbreviated, referring to "zaffra" (sapphire/cobalt) and "sol" (gold/the sun)</note> ...by the Lord who is King. Which is explained through the clarity of words <insert>namely, which is elsewhere in full</insert>.

<margin>A true philosopher</margin>
<margin>Substance</margin>
<insert>Morienus says</insert> <term>Alchemy</term> <note>original: "Alkyma"</note> is the science teaching how the genus of metals may be preserved in their proportions, passing into the earth by its own reason; it does not destroy the art, but deprives itself of it. <gloss>More difficult</gloss> toward sublimation, degeneration, and subtle coagulation, which I call.

<margin>The word Alchemy</margin>
<insert>Alkyma is called alchemy</insert> <term>Alchemy</term> is also the pure [light?] of Alexander... as much as it is called a worthy petition from the earth, or <term>alchemy</term> is the boldness of the elixirs... so that they do not pass into unworthy effects. It is, however, a thing of greatness and wonderful. An action gradually generating the eternal in earthly things, conferring upon earthly things the magnitude of all worldly <gloss>of the world</gloss> things.

# Here begins the prologue of the book of animation according to Master Alquidus

<margin>Alquidus <note>Likely a Latinized name for an Arabic authority, possibly Al-Kindi or a similar sage.</note></margin>
Let one Alquidus hold that which is called the perfection of the mind of God in the iron of things <note>original: "ferrum rerum"</note>, plucked from the herbs or by the multiplication of the work of divine things. Those who wish to trade in these matters must then watch over the destruction of things with vigilance. And the messenger of God is not able to multiply the life and variety of colors unless he first evidently names the perfect water. Or because he forms the world in which each man is led to his own true time, as you are advised. For there is given either a work of something or of boles <note>clays or medicinal earths</note>, which is therefore called that which we name to place. Otherwise, he will scarcely escape the damages of apoplexy <note>metaphorical for a sudden failure or "stroke" of the chemical process</note>. For color is the perfection of man; let it be according to the precepts of many. **Sulfur**. **Arsenic**. Silver <note>original: "Arrentum" for "Argentum"</note> which begins to be recovered at this time, which is shown to be healthy for the subscription of the work, so that it may change the color in each of its parts.

But the body will escape because they are silent from the <unclear>nature</unclear> of the earth; you have the color and the fiery strengths. **Salt**, however, reddens just like water poured out in burning. And they have to break the same thing which is not seen but lies hidden in the color. It bears a red color when so many graces are applied to enjoy the excess. **Atramentum** <note>Vitriol or black ink-sulfate</note> is first from the whiteness by fire or evaporated at midday, brought through or through redness just as it finishes in the day. **Quicksilver** <note>original: "Argentum vivum"</note> opens the way and effects a whitening color, but it induces a congruence or whiteness just as from the same salt. **Calamine** <note>Zinc ore</note> is so called when it is therefore of value for things at midday. **Cimantes** <note>possibly a corruption of "simentes" or "ciment"</note> or a certain **Magnesia** or **Salt** does that just as alcohol <note>original: "alchois," here referring to a fine powder</note> in greenness; afterwards the same is led to a gold color or into various colors. **Cinnabar** gives a gold color through a clear brightness. **Dichinces** <note>an obscure mineral term</note> however in burning, which is found in the truth of the stone. **Calamine** varies because through falsehood it had reached the same, or when the color of things recedes most swiftly. **Alum** which is white changes all moderations. Just as **Magnesia** slips away, **Urine** or yellow-red just as it has in the eggs; afterwards it effects gold because it is associated with **Coral**. From the whiteness of coral, which when it is united with some of the gods, it has a fierce display. **Alkali salt** is gathered in moderation, but for many it is then after. **Almagra** <note>Red ochre</note> or lead-earth <note>original: "xplubru[m]" for "ex plumbo"</note>, it is then a living force when something is effected. It proceeds by one clean path of lead and is supplied. Gold or the iron-mine, let us wash the **Almagra** because it is of the times, or when it has a tendency more toward redness. **Vermilion** is of great value in noble work. **Sal ammoniac**, however, when rubbed with the earth, which for two or for any of the modes of colors, is demolished from a certain thing. **Sulfur**, which is a branch or remaining efficacy, delivers the body; the multiplication of living things lies in the way, renewed a little in my own way. **Adul** <note>possibly "Adrop" or another alchemical deck-name</note> or void in the earth, or held for the sake of things, that is the same as the iron through the food. Here it will be in the sum to see the color of the herbs. But a gradual color is seen as a remedy.

<meta>This page continues a technical alchemical treatise, focusing on the creation of the "Stone of Love" and "Amethyst" through the purification of gold and the use of sulfurous compounds. The Latin is heavily abbreviated and contains several "Decknamen" (code names) for chemical substances.</meta>

No one should doubt the excellence of the cut stone <note>original: "sýcisse," likely from the Greek 'schistos' for split or cut</note>, the son of Semez Rabaidro <note>A cryptic alchemical name, possibly of Arabic or Syriac origin, referring to a specific mineral or master</note>, where it is called the "Amethyst," which is then called in Latin the **Stone of Love** <note>original: "lapis amoris"</note>; nor is it ever found in its first form, but rather it follows the path of silver.

### **J**ust as if one were to work truly through the secure golden way: it is prepared through the earth, not through the whole, until it takes on a white color. For this is the quality of the earth for the sake of the coming work, where it is changed so that the color is dissolved; now it is said that it is only made for the regeneration of the thing, at the same time as the moisture. ->**Epilogue**<-

**A**nd so, by this process, the spirit is bound in the body, and the light is drawn from the shadows, so that the hidden may be made manifest through the art of the ancients. The work is great and requires a long time, but the dignity of the result is even greater. ->**concerning the Amethyst**<-

<margin>Epilogue</margin>
<margin>7</margin>
### **F**irst, the gold is added to the alum <note>original: "alūbo," likely alumen</note>, which leads to the true sweetness of the faith <note>A metaphorical term for a successful chemical reaction</note>. The work must be done with care, so that the body is opened and the spirit is fixed. When the mixture is firm, let it be dissolved for a long time, until it becomes like a thick ointment. Then, let it be poured out and extracted, so that the joy of the work may be seen. If it is poured out three times, it is said to be purified. This is the great mystery of the work, which is given to those who seek the truth of gold. If the first part is blessed, the whole will be perfected. ->**The Amethyst**<-

<margin>su</margin>
<margin>nu</margin>
### **T**his is the path through the thread of the many-colored stone, which is prepared by fire.
**H**ere the form is made complete. Another addition of silver is made, and the faith is led to a higher state. The mixture must be watched closely, so that the recognition of the colors is not lost. The spirit is mixed with the body, and the figure is fixed. Let the silver be added to the gold, and let them be joined together until they are pure and shining like a star. This is the recognition of the work, which is supported by the sulfur and the fire.

<margin>su</margin>
<margin>nu</margin>
### **W**hich is indeed the rule for the tin <note>original: "stagnum"</note> of **its Amethyst**, which must be melted five times.
The gold is purified through the fire, as is the custom of the art. Let the sulfur be added to the gold, and let it be burned until it is consumed. This is the way to make the gold soft and obedient to the hand of the artist. The recognition of the work is certain if the gold remains firm and does not flee from the fire. Let the mixture be macerated and then placed in the vessel. The work is then finished with the addition of the gold, and the form is made warm and bright. You shall place it in a secret location, where it may be kept safe until the solution is complete. This is a very worthy secret of the salt, which must be guarded with great care, so that the truth of the work may stand firm.

<meta>This page continues the metallurgical themes of the previous page, shifting from the preparation of realgar and whitening techniques to a narrative account of an encounter with a "Moor" (a practitioner of Islamic alchemical traditions) and specific recipes for "aurolium" and "elidrum" (alloys resembling precious metals).</meta>

A certain smith, while traveling, happened to be in his workshop with a certain Moor <note>original: "maurus"; likely referring to a practitioner of Islamic alchemy, which was highly influential in Europe at this time</note>. The Moor took two silver pieces in his hand and gave them to the smith, asking him to melt them in the fire. To these, he [the Moor] added a certain powder of a green color. A vigorous smoke arose, and in an instant, it appeared in his hand as if made of gold or silver <note>The text is slightly unclear here: "facies de gerū aut sulu[?] orū"</note>. And after the skill of the hands was demonstrated, he returned that artificial [product]. Whereupon, when that gold was examined by experts, it was found to be good and true. The Moor then gave them this way of making the "pharmacy of the Moors" <note>original: "faraciam maurorū"</note> with the same solvent. Finally, the Moor, being moved, revealed the secret of the powder they had received, saying that he could make much gold through it... 

<insert>¶</insert> Aurolium <term>aurolium: a gold-colored pigment or "counterfeit" gold alloy used in illumination and decorative arts</term> ought to be pulverized in this way: let lead be dissolved in a vessel... so that it might receive the lead from the other part... so that it may carry the gold into the mixture.

<insert>¶</insert> ...take iron filings <note>original: "limatū", likely "limatura ferri"</note>... and let them stand in the sun for two days. Afterward, take vinegar and pour it upon the filings; let another vinegar be added, and let it be done until all the filings are dissolved and reduced into a very fine powder.

<insert>¶</insert> And let this be mixed with others, and let it be washed with pure water until the salt is removed and the water comes out pure.

<insert>¶</insert> Elidrum <term>elidrum: a phonetic variant of "electrum," a naturally occurring or artificial alloy of gold and silver</term> which is an imitation of gold and silver. It is made from two parts of silver, one part gold, and one part copper; and Elidrum is the same as electrum.

<insert>¶</insert> For Elidrum from silver: take 3 parts of silver and one of gold... in a robust pan... until it becomes ceruse <term>cerussa: white lead, often used as a base or pigment</term>... and if done in another manner, it becomes Elidrum. When you add gold to this, it will become the best work. <insert>¶</insert> Aurolium, or gold for whitening silver, is made from... [the following lines are highly abbreviated metallurgical instructions involving lead, powders, and heating].

<meta>This page continues the metallurgical focus of the previous section, moving from the anecdotal account of the "Moor" to specific laboratory procedures involving tutty (zinc oxide), arsenic, and the whitening or "coloring" of metals. <margin>What it is</margin>
A whiteness <note>original: "Albedo"; likely a specific white substance or the state of the material</note> with egg whites until it becomes soft like a paste, and you should place it in protective vessels and then in water over a first-degree fire <note>a low, gentle heat</note>, and let it be thus so that it is spread out for 2 hours. Afterward, for two hours of strong fire, let it be dried into the metallic seed. From that protective arsenic, at a weight of 1 [measure] of the experiment over 10 [measures] of molten copper, it comes out white.

<margin>See tutty</margin>
Concerning tutty <term>tutty: crude zinc oxide collected from the chimneys of smelting furnaces, used to color copper or whiten metals</term>, see... grind the tutty well... then enough, and then apply "thunders" <note>original: "tonitrua"; likely a term for a violent chemical reaction or a specific volatile additive</note> and leave it in the fire for a day. Through 7 degrees <note>referring to increasing stages of heat</note>, then wash with fresh water until the bitterness is gone, then add enough so that it is like milk. The powder of tutty should afterward be in "the moon" <note>original: "luna"; the alchemical name for silver</note>; it gives it quality and brightness.

Regarding the separation of tutty: with tutty and oil of [blackness?]... dissolved, then finally it emerges; and sublime <note>to heat a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again, a process used for purification</note> it just as you sublimated "the sun" <note>original: "solem"; the alchemical name for gold</note>... 
<margin>Calcine</margin>
On the calcination <term>calcination: the process of heating a substance to high temperatures in air to achieve decomposition or oxidation</term> of tutty: calcine the tutty in an iron pot in a firmly closed vessel and afterward sprinkle it with enough water or sweet vinegar.
On the gumminess of tutty: with tutty mixed with wine... and vinegar in the sun, and sublime it to the second degree.
<margin>That it separates</margin>
Also, soak the tutty often until it is such that it is dissolved in double its amount of vinegar until it [glows?] three times in the water through fire for 4 days and nights. Afterward wash away the salt until it is fresh... then from the arsenic of flint... then soak it with enough water.
<margin>Sublime</margin>
Separate and sublime when the whiteness emerges with the dregs to the right... let it be whitened like silver and wax it with enough water... it is dissolved in distilled [fluids?] and the stone which is the "white [stone] of the eight philosophers" over the fire, and cast it upon the egg <note>original: "ovem"; literally 'sheep', but context suggests a scribal error for 'ovum' (egg) or 'aes' (copper)</note> and tin <note>original: "iove"; referring to the planet Jupiter, symbol for tin</note> if it should come into the "moon" <note>Silver</note> of magnesia, and as of tutty and realgar <term>realgar: a red arsenic sulfide mineral</term>.

<margin>To be heated</margin>
This tutty must be heated by fire until it is of a fiery color, and then it receives this color afterward when it is treated with the best vinegar and then dried many times; by heating it and grinding it with vinegar, which you shall do seven times or more, it liquefies more often upon copper <note>original: "ere"</note> if it is mixed with tutty to be dissolved; either [it becomes] red in color and draws gold, for without this medicine, when the powder of tutty is placed in the fire, it evaporates and leaves no redness of its own. Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> says this very solution coagulates as if it were perennial. Because the Philosopher, in speaking of the "friendship" <note>original: "amicitia"; refers to the chemical affinity or attraction between substances</note> [of substances], says regarding tutty with a solution from clay... 9 degrees water, and let it drink this when washed; then it becomes red, cherished in the body, then it drinks this just as you [see] a quick, firm fixation.

<margin>In the sayings of the philosophers</margin>
<margin>a</margin> **Ros** <note>original: "Ros"; likely referring to the "Rosarius Philosophorum," a famous alchemical treatise, or the word for "dew"</note>: Whoever wishes to join this art with two textiles <note>likely filters or woven materials used in the process</note>, make water and afterward earth and a form <note>original: "foru[m]"; possibly a mold or furnace</note> and all [the rest].

<margin>A</margin> **Alphidius** <note>a commonly cited Arabic alchemical authority in medieval texts</note>: Since the body <term>corpus: the solid metallic or mineral base of a substance</term> is first purged and calcined <term>calcination: the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder or oxide</term>, then that which is unified is that in which you wash; then the spirit <term>spiritus: a volatile substance or the gaseous "essence" of a material</term> itself is combined, and thus they make it firm.

<margin>P</margin> **Plato**: Since the body is purged and dissolved, then they smear the spirit into that same dissolved [matter]; then there is a total joining of what you desire, but it cannot separate for you because first the spirit is dissolved over the body; then a close joining occurs which the fire can still separate.

<margin>Ar</margin> **Aristotle**: The body is the spirit which is evaporated and which they have as a residue like earth, because they are a body changed into whatever it wanted; then it is coagulated with them, and a firm joining is made with them; then its spirit empties everything, then the coagulated things in them are firm coagulations.

<margin>G</margin> **Galen**: Prepare the body in a prepared "spirit-day" <note>original: "amĩo die"; possibly a specific astrological or chemical timing</note> in which the matter corrupts until the white becomes white and the red becomes red <note>referring to the alchemical stages of albedo and rubedo</note>; then, having been dissolved in water, and you should congeal <note>original: "roggelate"</note> those spirits over the washed body, and then it is thus white, or silver, much better than that which [is unclear]. Here he says "earth" then, which the author calls a "species" <note>original: "specie"; a specific alchemical ingredient or substance</note> against our body, which excels the body with strength and with spirit, and sometimes a divine part prepares it so that it may be better heated; then the earth is white.

**Hermes**: Wash the body with lime and hot water—not [too] hot, because it is easy to corrode the body with moisture; then the [impurities] that are in them should be removed; he ought to correct all dross and corruption; then when they are washed... [re-cast?] against it by species and by part... then from the matter it can be touched or seen.

**Ovid**: Light-making <note>original: "lumagutium"; likely a term for making a metal brilliant or enlightened</note> is done in ten ways; two [are] so that you may dissolve the body over water, or let the species dissolve in "baths" <note>original: "thurmes"; likely referring to 'thermas' or chemical baths</note> common with water, or let it dissolve the body and the "baths" species because one then is better than all, just as you would dissolve with the "baths" species, or it is said: "Fasten the body with water."

**Agnes the philosopher** <note>possibly a corruption of Anaxagoras or a reference to a female alchemist</note>: Dissolve the body and the species when they cannot be separated from the matter even by fire; but animal salt and other salts and other things should not be added so that the solution may become better, because the solution makes things closed; because [it is] wretched and one... moistens with water... so they say you should drench the spirits of the body... toward itself by calcinations.

# **Also, how it may be made malleable and red**
Iron vessels should be used. Take red honey from the month of May <note>Honey collected in May was considered by alchemists to have special vital properties due to the spring bloom.</note> in a new earthen pot; place it over the fire as you wish so that the honey is cooked, and afterwards let it stand and boil entirely in this way. Afterwards, remove all of it from the fire and place it in a cool spot so that it cools further until the next day; do this for seven days, with the honey being renewed daily. At the end, make it boil as before. Let it stand for seven days just as you did with the honey. Afterwards, you should add <unclear>dami</unclear>. Mix it with chicken blood for seven days, with the blood being renewed daily. Thus, the pot is turned again, but not placed on the fire. And in this blood, do not read of the brambles <note>original: "rubis"; likely referring to blackberry or raspberry bushes used in similar recipes</note> which, if it has many, this is done through a day by the light before a lead cover; and at the bottom of the pot, place a little clay as if it were wasted. Afterwards, place the silver in the pot and above it place "bows" made of bull’s bone <note>original: "oslo tauri"; likely "osso tauri"</note> and cover the pot well and carefully. And after this, let the pot stand in the lead... remove it from the fire and place it in a cauldron where there is water so that it boils, and in this way the operation is perfected for gold; it is not reduced to perfection unless it is stabilized... the outside of the pot... and this.

# **Concerning the wisdom you shall have regarding the plant called Lunaria**
Briefly, you will see how great the Moonwort is <note>original: "Lunaria"; a plant traditionally associated with the moon and alchemy, believed to open locks or transmute metals.</note>, whose leaves are of a celestial color; you will want those leaves. This herb is born from the new moon until the full moon, producing one leaf every day. In the middle of the lunar cycle, on the fifteenth day, the herb is full; when the moon wanes, one leaf is removed every day until it is stripped of its leaves and falls to the earth. From the juice of this herb, at the very end of the plant, make it boil with quicksilver <note>original: "argentum uiuum"; mercury</note> and it will become the Red Stone <note>The "lapis rubeus" or Red Stone is the final stage of the Philosopher's Stone, capable of transmuting base metals into gold.</note>. And place this stone upon silver and it will become the gold of the earth as mentioned before. This herb grows on the banks of rivers and in mountains; its leaf is round in the manner of two [coins?], the wood is reddish. Its flower is waxen. Its odor is like the odor of musk, and it has milk like the <unclear>actu</unclear> <note>Likely "tithymalus" or spurge, known for its milky sap.</note>. Take the water... where when the end... it is so excellent for this purpose. Take <unclear>xpoc</unclear> upon the silver and it will become the best gold... so that the silver becomes gold. If you place this gold upon lead, it is gold. Regarding the roots of this herb... it makes the end powerful... it softens well... if you place it during the moon. It becomes a stone. From the dried leaves... the gold of the earth... take the king for the day from the foam... well, do not place it for seven days... all the white hairs of your body will fall out and in their place black hairs will be born <note>A common alchemical claim that certain elixirs could rejuvenate the body, reversing the signs of aging.</note>.

<summary>This page details two primary alchemical processes: the use of May honey and chicken blood to make silver malleable and "red," and the harvesting of the Lunaria plant to create a "Red Stone" for transmuting silver into gold and rejuvenating the body.</summary>

# Following the Mastery of Waters

If you wish to make **burning water** <note>original: "aquam ardentem"; a term for concentrated alcohol or a strong acid capable of combustion</note>, put **wine of lime** <note>original: "calic' vinū"; wine treated with quicklime to increase its potency or alkalinity</note> in a pot so that it can take in as much water as the lime absorbs, and let it overflow a little above it. Let it sit for eight days; afterward, if you wish to work with it, take that which floats on the top, either for coloring metals and other such things that are within, or for the first water.

<margin>Of red water</margin>
Another water is made from wine in the same quantity: take a portion of the wine and put it in a round pot; place it in the furnace and leave it for one day. Afterward, take it out and pour twice as much **strong vinegar** <note>original: "aceto forti"; highly concentrated acetic acid</note> over it. Leave it for three days, and when you wish to work with it, take the decoction that floats on top and work with it.

Another water is made from **ceruse** <note>original: "cerusam"; white lead</note>: grind it and put it in a pot. Leave it in the pot and place it in the furnace for four hours. Afterward, take the matter and add twice as much strong vinegar. Leave it for three days; afterward, when you wish to work with it, that which floats on top will be **green water**.

Another water is made from **verdigris** <note>original: "viride eris"; literally "green of copper"</note> and with sulfur; grind them together and put them in a pot. Close the vessel with the **lute of wisdom** <term>lute of wisdom</term> <note>original: "luto sapientiae"; a specialized alchemical sealant made of clay, dung, and hair used to airtight-seal vessels</note>. Place it in the furnace and leave it for two hours. Afterward, take the matter and pour twice as much strong vinegar over it. When you wish to work with it, take what floats on top and use these waters in place of azure water <note>original: "aqua azūri"; a blue pigment or solution</note> for the coloring of divided leaves.

These four waters strongly produce an acid for the treatment of youth in the water of another small lead <note>original: "plumelle"; likely a diminutive of *plumbum*</note> or for things decorated with lime.

**Mars** <note>the alchemical name for iron</note> is thus purified by the smoke of... and sulfur over **Venus** <note>the alchemical name for copper</note>; it becomes red and purified. Afterward, take <insert>amber</insert> <note>original: "lugarum"; likely a resin or yellow mineral</note>.

<margin>Concerning the whitening of copper</margin>
If you wish to paint with gold and... in an open vessel; afterward take wine and put it in such earth, placing the **silver** <note>original: "argentum"</note> there. It will be re-washed and be of great value; some of the aforementioned matter will dissolve in the fire. Return it to that water of wine and then to... until it becomes soft. In this liquid, silver becomes soft; when it has been made soft, place it in the crucible and during this time it will be restored, giving it its color. Afterward add half as much silver; if it has congealed, place it on a clean cloth dipped in water... it will become clear or bubble; use it with **tartar** <note>original: "tartaro"; potassium bitartrate, a byproduct of winemaking used as a flux or cleaning agent</note> dissolved in water.

<header>The Softening of Copper [A]</header>

Take the urine of boys and the sharpest vinegar, and mix them together with Alexandrian vitriol <note>original: "vitrioli alexandrini"; a hydrated sulfate of copper or iron used for etching and dyeing</note>, good euphorbium <note>original: "euforbij"; a caustic plant resin</note>, and also bad, stinking sulfur which is foul and red. Prepare this until it is reduced to the appearance of milk. Then take the copper and treat it until it becomes soft. It should be soaked in this for a long time, so that the copper alone is saturated until it sustains a thick color. This is done with an equal weight of the mixture. Put the copper in a small amount of water so that it does not evaporate, or by irrigation. It is then cleaned with salt and sand until it becomes white. Afterward, it must be washed to complete the work. <margin>Solution</margin>

# Dissolution is done of lead in various ways <insert>at that time</insert>
Sometimes it is done in horse dung <note>original: "stercore equino"; decaying horse manure was a standard laboratory heat source, providing a steady, gentle "compost" heat</note>. It is also done in a warm place, or in a water bath <note>original: "balneo aquae"; a bain-marie</note>. It can also be done in a pot full of boiling water, or in vinegar within closed vessels. <margin>How to collect thus</margin>

# Glue is made in this way
When you take wine, water, vinegar, and sulfur, mix them until they are combined. Alternatively, take cheese and warm it with water—not so it is squeezed, but so that the glue is expressed, which does not taste like mud. Another way is to take lime and mix it with egg white for the work.

# Another way: take flour and cook it 
and mix it with warm water or with egg whites.

# Of special glass
Special glass <note>original: "De vitro speciali"; likely referring to lead glass or a metallic glaze</note> is made by taking washed lead and treating it so it becomes like a shining leaden ball. Put this with the prepared matter in a glass vessel and reduce it through a process that makes it flow.

# Hardening iron
Take the juice of a radish <note>original: "raphanum"; radish juice was a common medieval reagent for tempering and hardening steel</note> and mix it with the juices of plants that are found there. Cast the iron into this to distill it, or bury it in the earth while the distillation is equalized. This can be done for a long time until it is ready for another use. <margin>The same</margin> This is done in the same way in water or in the future...

# Take the matter
Take the water and the matter, or take what you wish to burn... <margin>burn the grapes</margin> dissolve it in double its weight of strong vinegar and place it in a pot for a night. Then take it all in the benefit of the vinegar, and strain it through a very thick cloth. Let it sit for six or seven days, straining it and then letting it reside. When it has settled well at the bottom of the vessel for six days, it will be clear and delicate. <margin>H</margin> If you wish to calcine it, it is done with sulfur and strong water <note>original: "aqua forti"; nitric acid</note>, which sustains it.

### The Prologue begins
**A**ll of our knowledge, which from ancient books <insert>Here begins the first book of the Master</insert> we have found scattered throughout our own collection, <insert>Heber the Philosopher, King of the Persians,</insert> we have wished to gather into one brief summary <insert>on the art of alchemy</insert> because over three years it has been frequently simplified; it is sufficient in this edition that our book be a receptacle full of every defense <note>The author is framing the book as a definitive shield against error or criticism</note>, lest that which happens either before or at one time should make another manifest at the same time in this our volume. Thus, for the wise, this most excellent and noble part of philosophy shall be made open and fulfilled. Know, my son, that in this work the entire operation of the art is contained in these chapters; whatever is further disputed or needs to be reduced in the middle, we handle sufficiently. <insert>Note</insert> Let him know, however, that whoever is ignorant of these our ways is very far removed from our art, unless he holds the true root upon which the ancients founded their doctrine. <insert>Creation</insert> For he who is not truly a "son of the art" <note>original: "filia artis"; a traditional term for an alchemical initiate, though the scribe uses the feminine "daughter" here</note> has not attained it, nor can he complete the teachings of this art. He has, however, an easier path to the art, even if ignorance remains complete <insert>with</insert> regarding the mastery of this our work; yet for us, he who is remote from the reasoning of the art <insert>behold</insert> does not know how to perceive what is greatest for the generation and the manner of extraction and birth. First, I seek authority from him regarding all works, without which <term>philosophy</term> <note>meaning alchemical knowledge</note> cannot be known; our art in all its works follows nothing but <term>nature</term>, which it imitates. <insert>Friend</insert> Therefore, my son, reveal to yourself through the mind: he who wishes to be perfected in this art, which in almost all sciences is the most perfect of the hidden things, must desire to be changed. Therefore, work and study in the ways of the <term>King</term> <note>The "King" often refers to the perfected state of matter (gold) or the specific path of the Great Work</note>, always revolving within yourself through true doctrines and logical truths, which you ought to acquire if you wish to trust in our authority; you must draw out the errors of the erring and reveal them. Remaining in those things, you may be able to imitate nature in the craftsmanship of your work. <insert>Gift</insert> For he who has well-divided all things in time, which the craftsman possesses in the work, is hindered lest he should come to a perfected end. <insert>Behold</insert> Saying those things which constrain the craftsman, it is necessary to hold in the mind <insert>that</insert> what is disputable in the notation of the <term>sophists</term> <note>referring to "false" alchemists who use trickery or misunderstood logic</note> who, through their own ignorance, pursue a greedy mastery; they enter the art and soon after reply that it does not exist <insert>at once</insert> because all the voices of those who respond to them are corrected by us in such a way that the truth will be made plain enough to the aforesaid. .First part regarding the work.

<margin>
Obstacles of the matter
</margin>

We have determined here where we speak concerning the first mode, in which the reasoning of those helping with the work, both <insert>the whole king</insert> and their effective disposition, is summarized by the philosophers. **The fourth part narrates there how, concerning the disposition of this body**, those things which we have placed as material must first be understood by the practitioner <note>original: "xalēandū" (likely a corruption of "calculandum" or "exaltandum"); here referring to the one performing the operations</note>. It is necessary to reduce them with all their radiation and spirit to the first elements, which prevent obstacles in the order of the work from being reached.
### Thus, the obstacles hindering this work are generally twofold.

**B**ut because at the time of knowing, there is a lack or occupation of labors, and others in power, or the vanity of days on the part of the organs <note>the "organs" here refer to the physical body and the senses</note>, or laziness on the part of the soul. **On the part of the organ, it is said where the organ is either weak, distorted, or corrupt, or where there is a lack of the soul's portion.** For if the soul is pure in the organs, but the organ itself is full of fraud or fatigue, or if the life is such that fantastical delusions take over, one cannot receive the debt of this art; for they turn away from the light and move toward the opposite, choosing evil instead of the good.

### Concerning the obstacles on the part of the body

**I**t is now shown how and why this work has obstacles for a man, which are gathered here together. I say that if a man does not have his organs complete, he cannot be perfect for this work. For if he is blind or a hundredfold <term>curtatus</term> <note>original: "cyrcenit’ dēt r tūcatū"; likely meaning "truncated" or missing limbs</note>, he is not suited for the medical arts nor the touch of philosophy, nor can he be useful. If he is afflicted by a debt of bile <note>referring to the imbalance of the four humors</note> and is thus poorly regulated, or if he is one of those whose life is given to labor and art but whose seed is taken by avarice, he will not prevail. These people, by the condition of their bodies, are hindered from the pure life required for this work.

### Concerning the obstacles on the part of the soul

**W**e have premised the one cause in which we narrated the absolute mastery of the soul. **Obstacles on the part of the common and varied dependencies.** It remains to narrate briefly the obstacles on the part of the soul, which are the greatest inhibitors of this most complete work. I say, therefore, that when one has a physical organ but lacks reason or clarity <unclear>Balī pā</unclear>, then the foundations of the variations which we require cannot be held within them. Let it be known that such a person fears the true radiation or the light, for they endure in a mind that is empty of the truth which can be understood through reason.

## Sublimation, likewise of its living order <note>original: "uiuva eius ordinem," possibly referring to the "living" or "quick" state of the matter, such as quicksilver</note>, in its entirety without the loss of substances, etc.

**L**et us say, therefore, that <term>sublimation</term> <note>The process of heating a solid until it becomes a vapor and then collects again as a purified solid on a cooler surface</note> is like the removal of a thing from the earth. It follows that it is permitted for the "fat" <note>original: "pingue," often referring to the oily, sulfurous essence of the matter</note> to be raised to the heights of the earth, because they ought to be ordered. <margin>Sublimation</margin> **Sublimation, sweetening, and vivification** <note>original: "dulcificaco et viuificaco"; these processes aim to remove "acidity" or corrosiveness and restore the "life" or spirit to the metal</note> are said to be done in the sublime [manner]. Some are done with ignition, some indeed with a moderate fire, and some with a gentle fire, so that the matter of sulfurous fire may be sublimated; this is the one that, above all others, possesses fire. Since we have held this property, whoever shows one [substance] stronger and thicker [will succeed]. <margin>It is sublimated in iron vessels</margin> The whole vessel should be well closed for any purification, or rather for the blackening <note>original: "demigrone," likely "denigratio" or the Nigredo stage</note> of the <term>rebis</term> <note>original: "rebi," the "dual thing" or the philosophical hermaphrodite, representing the union of opposites like spirit and body</note> where the earth, as it is said, since it is always impure, will receive the necessary sublimations. They guard their own ingenuity so that the process of the figures is much more difficult, whatever you have done with any of the vials. It was clearly said that the vessel holding those [vapors] should keep the smoke suppressed and not let them escape outside. <margin>sublimation</margin>

It is necessary that the rising substance exhales, which belongs to the application of sublimation to the whole, proportionally, so that the substance ascends higher, becoming cleaner and more lucid over time, so that it may be clearly seen that it is cleansed from the earthy dregs. <margin>sublimation</margin> Further, it must be noted that what remained of the central part does not have [affinity] with the matter of fire. ### Chapter 15: On Calcination

<margin>The Sun and Moon <note>In alchemy, the Sun (Sol) represents Gold and the Moon (Luna) represents Silver.</note></margin>
Indeed, let us put forth the completion of the discourse on the account of distillation; we also wish to treat **calcination** <note>The process of heating a substance (usually a metal) to a high temperature in order to oxidize it or reduce it to a powder.</note>, and how calcination is perfected either by fire according to the extraction of the moisture of the consolidating parts and their reduction; but here it is calcined according to the reduction as the things to be calcined are calcined. Either the bodies are previously calcined by the spirits of other earths... all these are of the three [types]: **Silver** <note>original: "luna"</note>, because they are the bodies of two spirits, one visible like **Venus** [Copper] and **Mars** [Iron] and the **Sun** [Gold], **Moon** [Silver], and **Saturn** [Lead].

<margin>One calcination</margin>

The method is by means of a flask <term>ampoule</term> <note>original: "ampullam", a round glass vessel used in alchemy</note> with the substances pressed down even to the neck, as far as it allows [the worker] to count. ### Concerning the Triple Distinction of Medicines

<margin>
threefold difference of medicines
of metals
</margin>
It is plain that there are three types of medicines in nature. One is of the **first order**, another of the **second**, and another of the **third**. Philosophers say that medicines of the first order are made through the art of minerals, which are diminished by the pouring out of their dregs. Others are of such a kind that they do not bring sufficient stability, which happens to be changed and corrupted by evaporation. This is because they have a total hold on the intermediate name.
Other medicines concern the **whitening of Venus** <note>original: "albaeia venīs". Venus is the alchemical name for Copper.</note> or **Mars** <note>Mars is the alchemical name for Iron.</note> which does not accept fixation. These move by the addition of color alone, either by the moon or the wind, and thus the art can be carried into the material. These do not change [the metal] unchangeably, for they do not stand, but are diminished through evaporation <note>original: "exalaced" (exhalatio)</note>.
But those of the **second order** of medicines are those parts which, though somewhat diminished, are yet perfectly prepared. They are different in some way, or are the whitening of those things which are entirely fleeting...

# 4. Beginnings

The roasting of the calcination <note>original: "assuacõis calciñ"; assuatio refers to a slow heating or "roasting" of a substance in a sealed vessel.</note> which we have taught until now should be carried out while hot. When it has become red, take the living mass of the material and dry it by means of sulfur, according to its alignment. In this way, however, let it be cleansed from all spiritual sulfur. It is said that we should turn this toward alignment twenty times, so that it is properly "capitated" <note>original: "capitat"; likely referring to the "caput mortuum" or the dregs left after distillation.</note>. Dissolve that in water, and then the dissolution will truly calcine that substance again. Let the dissolution suffice for the demonstration. After this, let the silver <note>original: "lune"; Luna is the alchemical name for silver.</note> be treated as was said.

<vocab>
**Roasting (assuatio):** a slow, dry heating process.
**Calcination (calcinatio):** heating a substance to high temperatures to cause oxidation or powdering.
**Solution (solutio):** dissolving a solid into a liquid state.
**Fixation (fixatio):** the process of making a volatile substance stable in fire.
**Silver (luna):** the alchemical metal associated with the moon.
**Iron (mars):** the alchemical metal associated with the planet Mars.
**Mercury (mercurius):** quicksilver, often considered the "spirit" of metals.
**Sulfur:** a prime alchemical principle representing soul or combustibility.
**Alchemy (alchimia):** the art of transmuting base metals into noble ones.
**Medicinal (medicinalis):** relating to the healing or transformative properties of the "philosopher's stone."
</vocab>

## Perquisites which are for the perfection from the examination in general

Regarding the majesty of God, we make no narration with all our free voice. Without any cunning of genius, the reason is the king and the mediator in all things. ## Concerning the Examination of Four of Them by Cements

**Let** us say, therefore, that some of them [the metals] once [show] more in the examination of cement, but others less. If this heating should occur through a single setting of the sun, where the day is fashioned to be joyful, the vessel must be held so that no persuasion <note>interference or air</note> exists. If you have placed those things in the earth, we see the body joined in the manner of a stone. And then, let that earth be well-calcined <term>Calcined: reduced to powder through high heat</term> to the dregs of another vessel in this moisture. The air is already well-circulated in time, and you shall see the vessel of the philosophers well-closed. Indeed, in the furnace of the philosophers, you shall approach the philosophical wood <note>original: "rignum phicum," likely a specific type of fuel or a metaphor for the heat source</note> in the manner of the philosophers, through which for a space of twenty-one days it should be burning. The fire before the philosopher is such that it is one with the twofold preparation, but not with the mass from that part; it will be entirely placed with two olive leaves <note>original: "folis olivarum," potentially used as a measure of heat or a specific fuel for a gentle flame</note>. For not otherwise is it through the fire of combustion which compels it to endure. When these days have passed, extract the aforesaid vessel from the furnace, and dry that which you find inside. Afterward, I wish you to take one part of that thing with ten parts of clean material... anoint one part in the given <unclear>mummial</unclear> matter with one part in the clean... concerning the reception of these mixtures, all of them as one, add one of them differently so that it is mixed into one for all. Make from it a flow. Here it is dispersed if the white <insert>white</insert> remains in it where it was in its nature. You will now find it to be of two faces; here the magnitude is fulfilled. Here, in the manner in which the white is rolled in every clean world, another dyer <note>original: "tinctor," a substance that changes the color/nature of the metal</note> enters the soul of its mixture into its body. If you study to join it to a foreign body, you labor in vain; for the truth is more clear than the shore. If the white is not empty, you have seen it, and the Lord shall receive the soul of his philosophers into his hand.

And as he will show the "paspazi" <note>original: "paspazī"; likely a specialized alchemical term for a "universal" or "all-encompassing" distillation</note> distillation, saying: distill the spirit of spirits by the wind in the breast <note>A reference to the Emerald Tablet: "The wind carried it in its belly"</note> into the smoothing air. Four distillations are effective by themselves; they carry an ounce... it is of great value.
Some place this distillation here in liquid things, but it had the name of the "distillation of sublimation" <term>sublimation: the process where a solid turns into gas and back to solid, used to purify spirits</term>. Four spirits they called by the name of "flow."
Likewise, as he will show, **coagulation** <term>coagulation: the thickening or solidification of a liquid</term> is a great thing. This was an ounce for the fixation <term>fixation: making a volatile substance stable under heat</term> so that he might show the grace of the spirit... as he said, it receives the "power of the superior and the inferior" <note>original: "vīm sūpīōrē atqz mferīōrē"; another reference to the Hermetic principle of "As above, so below"</note> because the inferior is joined with the superior oil, which they consume in this alembic <term>alembic: a type of still used for distillation</term>, joined in weight.
To this end, so that they may vent over the fire... apply the power to those things which are required for the appearance of the **Philosopher's Stone** <term>original: "lapidē phīad"; the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting immortality</term>,
estimating from one as if briefly in one of each work: he might demonstrate the whole. Because it is now compacted, then this is to be introduced to fixation over the fire.

### <insert>Concerning the calcination of the top of the alembic</insert>

**W**hat calcination is and how it is done is spoken of in this spirit.
Truly, to "calcinate" is the way of speaking by which the moisture of these spirits [is removed] by fire... and in that vision then it is perfectly joined. The spirit is for the burning smoke and for fixation over the fire and flux <note>original: "fluvīonēm"; the ability of a substance to melt and flow like wax</note>. If there is any other flight <note>original: "fūgīonē"; referring to volatility or the substance "escaping" the heat</note>, the matter will overcome all things and will penetrate. Know this from what he himself says.

### <insert>Concerning the works of distillation, of which [it was] previously said</insert>

**B**ecause of the length of the spirit and the difficulty in the complete, perfect operation, which must be performed, some [use] one process of regimen, some two, some three, and one proceeds to place the **elixir** <term>elixir: the refined medicinal or transformative substance sought by alchemists</term>.
For they calcinate the matter and afterwards they place it; some truly finish one, then they calcinate, dissolve, and distill, and afterwards they place the "wine" <note>original: "vīñ"; likely the *spiritus vini* or rectified alcohol used as a solvent</note>.
From this, nothing [unprofitable] emanates; it proceeds more clearly... the fruits of the divided processes with fire and with... both with one and...

Some do not doubt that they cannot proceed if they lose the way entirely, except with **fire**. Some, indeed, [proceed] with **solution** <term>solution: the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</term>, and some indeed by both. <gloss>The work of the work</gloss> Indeed, [some proceed] with the **calcination** of all things.

### For those who worked with fire alone, the process was twofold.

**I.** For some of them took the aforementioned matter and decocted <term>decoction: boiling a substance to extract its essence</term> each one separately by itself in vessels through **sublimation** <term>sublimation: heating a substance until it becomes vapor, then cooling it back into a solid to purify it</term>, always leading that which was "subtle" away from the "dense." They continued reducing that which was below until the whole was reduced into a **frog earth** <note>original: "terra rana"; a technical term for the thick, dark residue or "dregs" left at the bottom of a flask during the early stages of the work</note> that was thick. For by the office of fire, they added the "temperaments of the moon" <note>likely referring to silver or the cooling, moist qualities associated with the moon</note> which was like water, above the purified red rubies <note>original: "sup robes apura ribes"; this appears to be a repetitive technical formula or a scribal corruption referring to the "reddening" stage of the stone</note>.

### Another operation

<margin>4</margin>
**A.** Others, however, took the bodies [metals] previously prepared with spirits to be sublimated, and they fixed <term>fixation: making a substance stable so it no longer evaporates when heated</term> this earth. Afterward, they placed the washed bodies there; others used bodies calcined from the <unclear>...</unclear>. From these, they made a single "body" through **fusion** <term>fusion: melting substances together</term> in a vacuum, so that the **elixir** <term>elixir: the sought-after medicinal or transformative substance, often synonymous with the Philosopher’s Stone</term> might be made, similar to the purified red rubies.

### Another operation for the two

Those who worked with **solution** followed a twin path toward the one. They dissolved each [metal] separately and "milked" or extracted their waters until they reached the proper weights, and afterward, they coagulated <term>coagulation: the thickening of a liquid into a solid</term> them into a **stone**, and they said:

### The Elixir is the same

**A.** Other secret philosophers took all the aforesaid washed things and put them together and mixed them. Afterward, they dissolved and coagulated them. Some of these [used] only a solution of water through distilled water; they said these things would give a splendor. This is the splendor of the <unclear>...</unclear> through the solution from the aforementioned aggregate, everywhere a very clear water, which they afterward coagulated into a stone by the benefit of fire, and they said this was most true.

### For those who proceed with both, the way of the elixir was sevenfold.

<margin>1</margin>
For those who proceed with both [fire and solution], the way of the elixir was sevenfold. For some of them dissolved the bodies, and thus "bathed" by solution, they fixed them for sublimation. Others calcined the bodies and afterward dissolved them; they imbibed <term>imbibition: a process where a solid slowly absorbs a liquid</term> both. Thus, they dissolved the elevated things. Some calcined **quicksilver** <note>mercury</note> with the bodies and dissolved the same; they imbibed the liquor into a single vessel and dissolved it again.

# The second part of the present work, which is about the apparent minerals of metals.

I say to you now, with God’s help, that you may be able to act as an effective and proper practitioner, so that you may know the gathering of things to be congealed, both full and diminished. Without this knowledge, you cannot complete the work. Once these diminished things are managed without error, you will reach the goal that those above call the "healthy" and "diminished" [minerals]. No one should be ignorant of this in our work of completion.

For the **sickness** of the world <note>referring to the impurities in base metals</note> is more thoroughly diminished by the masters, and every body [of metal] must be reduced to health rather than a neutral state, since by the sacred law of our art it is possible <note>red mark</note> and easy. To the **sophists** <term>sophists: here referring to "false alchemists" who use trickery or "sophistry" rather than true chemical principles</term>, the truth of the secrets of the philosophers is hidden. They put forward a false fire, and because of these things, their inclination is not toward the truth. When their work begins, it does not endure; they are swallowed by the void of their own errors. They not only find this work difficult but impossible <note>red mark</note>.

Philosophy <note>original: "phia"; shorthand for Alchemy</term> does not call to those who are merely greedy for its reputation. They are like **garbage** <note>original: "garbage"; a term used by the scribe to denote the worthless "trash" results of false alchemy</note> because they are not sought out by the truth. They do not meditate, but they should know through medical experience that the reason for the beginning is found in the end, and experience is worth nothing without thought.

**Experience without meditation accomplishes little; for philosophers, experience is more than meditation.** <note>This reflects a core medieval scientific debate: whether "doing" is more important than "thinking." The author argues they must be combined.</note>

Therefore, one must strive with great experience in this matter, for the art is lost to the miserable and those who follow worldly sweetness. No one can experience this thing unless they are first instructed in how to found and melt the substances. Once the action has begun, let it not cease. If you do not achieve perfection at first, do not stop; proceed until the lightning-flash of success appears <note>red mark</note>.

Do not let the labor of your hands or the expense of the work deter you, for persistence conquers all. With the aid of God as our guide, you will receive the reward for the labor of your hands from these superior things <note>red mark</note>.

If you lack the reasoning for this work, distill it once from this water and congeal it for seven days.

<insert>On the nature and property of Venus</insert>

Venus <note>The alchemical name for Copper</note> in its height <note>original: "altitudine"; the external, observable properties of the metal</note> is hot and dry like the Sun, and of a red, fiery color—bitter, sharp, and masculine. In its depth <note>original: "profundo"; the hidden, internal essence or "soul" of the metal</note> it is cold and moist like the Moon and <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum"; Mercury</note>, white, weak, and feminine. On one side it is hot and moist, a bloody gold, sweet-smelling, and masculine; on the other side it is cold and dry. The Venus of the philosophers <note>Refers to the purified "essence" of copper sought by alchemists</note> prohibits quicksilver, <term>melancholy</term> <note>The "black" humor, here representing a cold/dry state of matter</note>, acid, and the cold seed.

<insert>On the nature and property of Mercury</insert>

<image-desc>Decorative initial in red ink representing the astronomical/alchemical symbol for Mercury (☿), consisting of a circle with a cross attached to the bottom and stylized crescent-like horns on top. It functions as the initial letter of the word 'Mercurius'.</image-desc> Mercury <note>The metal Quicksilver</note> in its height is cold and moist; it desires quicksilver and tin, a flowing water and a weak moisture, and is feminine. In its depth it is hot and dry, and constant against the cold, fiery, red, bitter, sharp, and masculine. On one side it is cold and moist, like lead or quicksilver, melancholy, black, acidic, and feminine. On the other side it is hot and moist, gold or bloody, and sweet.

<insert>On the nature and property of the Moon</insert>

The Moon <note>The alchemical name for Silver</note> in its height is cold and dry like Venus and hard lead; it draws <unclear>lanohea[m]</unclear> to the sensitive God <note>possibly a religious metaphor for the metal's responsiveness to heat</note>, and is feminine. In its depth it is hot and moist, gold or bloody, sweet-smelling, and masculine. On one side it is cold and moist, quicksilver, a flowing water, a weak moisture, and feminine. On the other side it is dry and cold, against the fire, red, bitter, acidic, and masculine.

---

<insert>On the nature and property of the Sun</insert>

The Sun <note>The alchemical name for Gold</note> in its height is hot and moist, and like bloody water, sharp, sweet, sweet-smelling, and masculine. In its depth it is cold and dry, the "Venus of the philosophers" and quicksilver, melancholy, black, acidic, and the cold seed. On one side it is dry and cold, of a fiery red color, bitter, acidic, and masculine. On the other side it is cold, and tin, quicksilver, flowing water, white, and weak. And all things are made clear to you in the figure of the seven—that is to say, in the figure of all the planets.

<meta>This page continues the alchemical discussion of the internal and external properties of metals. While the previous page focused on the mystical "heights" and "depths" associated with planetary correspondences, this page shifts to a more physical (though still theoretical) explanation of how different metals are born within the earth, focusing on the "Mercury-Sulfur theory"—the belief that all metals are composed of these two primary principles in varying states of purity and "cooking."</meta>

...because of their volatility <note>original: "fugacitatem"; the tendency of a substance to evaporate or escape when heated</note> from fire before it is joined, and it escapes during the testing of the [metallic] bodies after it is joined <gloss>as it seems</gloss> until it is purified. Because through the burning of sulfur and its combustion, the crushed heart is changed entirely; for example, gold [cannot be made] thus from quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> unless mixed with bright, clear sulfur in the heart of the earth, cooked for a long time by the moderate heat of the sun. And because it remained in this cooking for a great duration, that which was clear in it is preserved, lest it be driven to a harsh hardening or dried out; therefore it neither rots nor is easily consumed by fire.

## On the Origin of Silver

**S**ilver is made from clear quicksilver <note>mercury</note> mixed with clear white sulfur and pure red [sulfur], cooked in the heart of the earth, though not as much as gold. And because there was a reddish part in it, just as in the cooking, by enduring a long delay in the manner of gold...

## On the Origin of Copper

**C**opper is made from turbid quicksilver mixed with red sulfur, thick and hard... in the heart of the earth by moderate heat... and because it is in the decoction <note>the process of heating or "cooking" the mineral</note> for a long time, it then has nothing of the burning nor anything of the red... and is already an impure body in its own cause... because indeed it is easily burned by vinegar, its body then dissolves into a greenness, which is called the flower of copper <note>original: "flos cupris"; this refers to verdigris, the green pigment that forms on weathered copper</note>.

## On the Origin of Iron

**I**ron is made from quicksilver mixed with strong and thick sulfur, hard in the heart of the earth. The cooking is of another moderate force... having [the nature] of copper... because the heat of the fire is so great that it flows, and the heat... through long decoction, the parts constrain themselves to be mixed and it becomes hard; and when it comes to dissolution <note>melting</note>, it is not as easy as copper.

## On the Origin of Tin

**T**in is made from clear quicksilver mixed with a small amount of white, clear sulfur; the cooking time is short with moderate heat. If it were cooked longer, it would be transmuted into the finest silver.

## On the Origin of Lead

**L**ead is made from quicksilver with white and primarily red sulfur... it burns and then becomes red in color...

# Concerning the method of preparing salts and alums
<margin>The Beginning of the Salt</margin>
Likewise, we must see how the bodies of minerals, which are weak in their complexions and origins, are set free for their purification and exaltation <note>the process of raising a substance to a higher state of purity or power</note>, just as the preparation of materials is completed with God's help. I purify the body with water under a dissolving salt <note>original: "salum resolutivum"</note> and place the water [there]; if by means of a firm word <note>original: "mume fermo," likely a corruption of "mune firmo" or referring to a specific instruction</note> concerning the refluxing salt and the filtration of the water of the said matter.

### On the preparation of common salt, let it be done thus
<margin>SALT</margin>
From here, each body is dissolved very quickly. **Here**, [place the salt] in four parts of clear rainwater <note>original: "aque pluvialis"</note> and distill it through a filter; then cook this water in a glass vessel <note>original: "uas vitreum"</note> with a gentle fire <note>original: "igne leui"</note> until it is consumed and the salt "freezes" <note>original: "gelatur"; refers to crystallization as the liquid evaporates</note>. Do this three times. Now let the salt you have received be dried out and place it in a glazed jar <note>original: "olla in uetreta"</note> and close its mouth with sealing clay <note>original: "opalo luto"; 'lute' was a paste used to hermetically seal alchemical vessels</note>, smeared over so that it cannot breathe <note>leak air or vapors</note>. Afterward, let it dry well in the sun or by a slow fire. Then place it in a baker’s oven <note>original: "furno paniscale"</note> for a full night; then move it, take it out, and open the jar, and you will find the salt. Indeed, it will appear as if it were distilled; congeal it as above and do this three times until the salt does not take on any color and there is no dross <note>original: "scoria"; the stony waste matter or impurities</note>, which is better for the work of the matter; do this again and then until the end.

### On the decoction of the matter
<margin>SALT</margin>
**This** salt—place another portion in a new heated pot and cover it on all sides with water; cook it over the fire until the salt no longer increases in the water. When it has stopped crackling <note>original: "crepitare"; salt makes a popping sound when heated</note>, take the metal and let it rest; restore this salt here; it seems to be fragrant <note>original: "olentem"; possibly "nitentem" meaning shining</note>; after it has ceased, cover it and leave it for a long time on the fire; at last, you will find it red <note>original: "rubeum"</note>.

### Another preparation
**The salt** shall be distilled in water, and let the filth likewise be scraped away; afterward, distill it through a filter. Then cook it in a glass vessel over a light fire until the water is finished and the salt is coagulated at the bottom of the vessel. After it has been dried three times, let it be dissolved in pure old wine <note>original: "uinum antiquum purum"</note> and remember [to expose it] to the sun or through a furnace. Distill through a filter; cook with a gentle fire until the corners... <note>original: "anglos verue"; an unclear technical phrase possibly referring to the corners of the vessel or a specific astrological timing</note>. Thus, fourfold to the salt, add lime <note>original: "calcem"</note> prepared from the powder of soot for this decoction <note>the liquid produced by boiling</note>.

# Another way for sublimated Mercury.

Another way for sublimated mercury: if you take **living silver** <note>mercury</note> that is well cleansed with the juice of all sour apples and the juice of celandine <note>a yellow-flowered plant in the poppy family, often used in alchemical recipes for its "golden" sap</note> and the juice of fennel roots, with strong vinegar and a little salt added first; then let it be dried with the hands until it is rendered clean of everything, renewing the aforementioned liquid in every washing until it is left... then it will remain very white. Let it also be cooked for a day in seawater and thereafter consumed until a fourth part of it remains, so that it might properly be reduced to a fourth; soon it will be changed below into oil in strong wine vinegar; let it be dissolved with the addition of **sal ammoniac** <term>Sal ammoniac: ammonium chloride, a volatile salt used to clean metals or act as a flux</term> and afterwards distilled through a filter.

Likewise, let it be sublimated by gum ammoniac <note>a medicinal resin</note> and salt as above, by a third part, to the weight that is reborn from the earth with the salt of the earth and distilled through a filter, placing it into another vessel so that it may be sublimated.

### Egg Water for the Red Core

This is the "marrow" <note>original: "medula," referring to the yolk or the innermost essence</note> of eggs, boiled until it is as hard as stone, white and separated above, which appears in the manner of a pith. If it is placed by itself in another vessel, and with the juice receiving it, a red water and a saffron-colored foam are said to glide away. And then, having cast this away according to custom, and for the sake of **vivifying** <note>In alchemy, to "vivify" is to make a substance reactive, "alive," or spirituous</note> it in its "belly" <note>original: "ventre," the interior of the distillation vessel</note> for ten days, it is said to produce a red water which will distill in the shell of its belly. When set aside and distilled by itself, it is seen to distill red. But when this water is received through a medium, it becomes white by itself as it is received; it ought to be replaced upon its own **dregs** <note>original: "feces," the solid residue left after distillation</note> until it is finished. ### Oil of Sulfur

Take one pound of **sulfur** and evaporate it with two pounds of **white lime** and very strong vinegar. Then renew the lime above and renew the sulfur, grinding them in this way until the substance acquires the property of red. And when this vinegar is distilled into its own vessel, let it be captured and separated into another. It will be that which descends with **arsenic**. Before they undergo "correction," you shall move <note>or shake</note> it every day for ten days, up to fifteen days. 

Let it be nourished with pure vinegar. Let a fire be made in the wax <note>original: "cera"; this may refer to the process of "ceration," making a substance soft and fusible like wax</note> and let it be extinguished in the said vinegar every time. Then let it be ground in a **mortar** <note>original: "mozocho," a variant of *mortario*</note> and immediately mixed with the said vinegar and placed by the fire. Repeat this every day until the whole force of the moisture is dissolved in the same vinegar, and the vinegar itself looks like the **blood of rubies**. Then place it in a distillation vessel and distill it, returning it upon its dregs until the most red liquid distills from it. Keep this for your work. Then take the other half that was treated and add a fourth part of **sal ammoniac** <note>original: "sal' arni," a common ammonium salt</note> and **vitriol** <note>original: "virol'," likely iron or copper sulfate</note> and roast them.

# Separation of Gold

This is concerning the separation from gold that has been very finely filed and prepared; it is placed in water <note>original: "aq[ue]"; likely referring to a corrosive solvent like aqua regia used to dissolve gold</note> over a red-filed residue and dried by the fire with honey <note>original: "mellite"; honey was sometimes used in alchemy as a carbon source or a binding agent</note>. # Separation of the Two and the Third

This concerns tin and filed silver: the separation of the two parts with a third part <unclear>added</unclear>. Take two parts of tin, because for one heart <note>original: "cor"; likely referring to the central essence or a specific ratio unit</note>, two are separated by way of the **dung-bath** <term>fimus: a bed of fermenting horse manure used by alchemists to provide a gentle, steady, and long-lasting heat</term>. First, proceed in a similar cause as if through a conduit from here to the full amount. In the logic of separation, it is perhaps a medicine <term>medicina: in alchemy, this refers not to a drug, but to the "elixir" or reagent that has the power to transform or "cure" base metals into noble ones</term> on its own, until it does not evaporate. Afterward, you should wash this salt from it with sweet water <note>original: "aqua dulci"; fresh water, as opposed to salt water or acidic solvents</note> and dry it. Then, place it to redden with common salt, a separation through and through, but only in a glass vessel that is finely **encrusted** <unclear>incrustratum</unclear> and well-sealed <note>original: "percluso"; hermetically sealed to prevent the "spirit" of the metal from escaping</note> so it does not "breathe out." Place it in the dead of the most heated manure for two days, by which logic, just as in the night, it is made into a lime <term>calx: the powdery residue left after a metal has been roasted or "calcined"</term>. Use sweet water so that all saltiness entirely recedes from it, even if you wash it with sweet water from the **papyrus** <note>original: "paperidem"; this may refer to a filter made of papyrus or a specific botanical additive</note>. Set it in the accustomed manner and you will see your white lime like our snow; the logic is to let it fail <note>i.e., settle or react</note> in the sun, which is the best for this purpose.

# Separation of the Man

This concerns human blood and gold, which is divided from a third part of the "heart" into one part. Cast it in every turn with the **arctic** <note>original: "artico"; possibly a reference to a "cold" quality or a specific north-pointing alignment in the lab</note> toward the medicine. Similarly regarding the medicine, thus place it above to burn the core part; by this logic, hold the medicines that whiten. Make it the "new daughter" of **calcined mercury** <note>original: "mercurii de calcinatoris"</note> and set it for a night. In every turn, make it glowing hot, and at another time through the **bath** <unclear>balneum</unclear> <note>original: "balne"; likely a water bath (balneum Mariae)</unclear>. Take the root of the branch <note>original: "radice sermeni"</note> and let it descend; then cast it through the **mercurial water** <note>original: "aquam mersalis"</note> and all of it with very strong vinegar in the hot sun until it is perfectly reddened. Its weight is the "root," and it reveals its art in the red; do the rest just as was previously done with the gold. ->Separation of the Man<-

# Separation of the Man

This is the "Man" separated and refined; you should separate it in salt water four times... <note>The text here becomes more repetitive and technical, focusing on the cycles of washing</note> and hence with salt water to the two parts. Take and dry its weight, and take of its medicine of the Sun <note>original: "solis"; alchemical code for gold</note> and of separated lead, and by the logic of the medicine, take one part of silver to the weight of the lime. In one work, separate the "son" <note>original: "filium"; perhaps a secondary product of the reaction</note>, consuming it with salt water according to the part for the salt of the medicine through the night. If this shines, it departs from it, for the medicine is no less quick. Wash the salt from it with distilled vinegar, then prepare and <unclear>dry it</unclear>.
